claims.text: Nanoparticles containing five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios maintain a stable single-phase solid solution across 473–1923 K.
High configurational entropy is responsible for maintaining the stable solid solution.
High configurational entropy kinetically suppresses rapid elemental diffusion and phase segregation.
Even slight compositional imbalances cause earlier elemental segregation or phase separation under otherwise identical operating conditions.
The initial nanoparticles are homogeneous, single-phase solid solutions.
Equiatomic and compositionally deviated nanoparticle batches can be compared under identical thermal cycling and operational conditions.
The relevant operating interval is 473–1923 K under controlled catalytic and thermoelectric environments.
Maintained phase homogeneity and uniform elemental distribution mediate the relationship between configurational entropy and stability.
Configurational entropy thermodynamically favors a random, well-mixed phase in equiatomic nanoparticles.
A slight departure from equiatomic composition reduces configurational entropy.
The entropy reduction caused by slight compositional imbalance enables enhanced diffusion and elemental redistribution.
Enhanced diffusion and elemental redistribution drive phase separation or surface segregation at high temperature.
Equiatomic nanoparticles will retain a homogeneous single phase and uniform elemental distribution over the operating range.
Compositionally deviated nanoparticles will show phase segregation or surface enrichment at lower temperatures than equiatomic nanoparticles.
The equiatomic baseline does not undergo significant phase change under mild thermal conditions or low-stress cycling.
The prediction applies when elemental-diffusion kinetics are limiting relative to the thermal-cycling timescale.
Conditions that substantially alter diffusion rates or surface energies may invalidate the prediction.
Segregation onset and phase transformations may depend on metal identity, nanoparticle size, and environment.
TEM, XRD, and XPS/EDS measurements can be used to compare phase structure and elemental distributions in the two batches.
Observation of equally stable, homogeneous single phases in both batches throughout 473–1923 K would falsify the proposed composition-dependent stability prediction.

contradictions.description: The stable category includes both equal and near-equal compositions, while the unstable comparison is defined as an even slight deviation from equiatomic composition. These categories overlap because no quantitative boundary distinguishes 'near-equal' from 'slight compositional imbalance.'
